transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-25
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Janelle Wu (Redwood SE optional), Mina Park (AuroraSearch - Head of Search), Liam O'Connor (AuroraSearch - SRE), Priya Rao (AuroraSearch - PM)

Summary: quick demo of hosted embeddings + rerank. showed API calls, console snippets, and a sample rerank pipeline. discussed security and perf. next: benchmark and pricing.

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. um we have about 45 minutes, we'll go through a short overview, then Ethan will demo the embeddings and rerank endpoints and then we'll talk about integration patterns and next steps.
[00:18] Mina: thanks, Sofia. excited to see how this could help our relevance issues. we've been getting a lot of low-precision results on our product search.
[00:26] Sofia: yeah great context, and if you could briefly outline current stack maybe that helps — do you still use Elastic as your primary index?
[00:33] Mina: yep, Elastic 7.x, some custom rescoring rules, and a small in-house model for category boosting. latency is about a 120ms median for search layer but the neural rerank is slow, it's a lambda and adds like 200-300ms per query.
[00:49] Ethan: okay thanks, that matches what we typically see. we'll show hosted embeddings for candidate retrieval and then the rerank endpoint which takes candidates + query and returns scores so you can reorder. the idea is keep the cheap filter in Elastic and use rerank for the top-K to reduce compute.
[01:03] Mina: can you show the API? pseudo-code would be great.
[01:08] Ethan: sure. first step is call /v1/embeddings with text batch to get vector for the query and for any documents you want to index. sample payload — vector size 1536 in our demo model but that's configurable; you can also use Redwood's embeddings with float16 quantized storage if you want smaller storage.
[01:27] [00:30] Ethan: then you do ANN lookups in your vector store (we demo with Pinecone and also show approximate brute force) to get top 200 candidates. next, call /v1/rerank with the query and the topK candidates. our rerank accepts either raw text or precomputed embeddings; it returns a ranked list with scores and optional explain tokens.
[01:49] Priya: is the rerank a separate model behind the endpoint or is it the same as the embedding model?
[01:55] Ethan: good q. technically it's a separate tuned model optimized for pairwise relevance — so embeddings for retrieval, rerank model for scoring. that lets you pick different tradeoffs — smaller embedding model for index size and a larger reranker for accuracy.
[02:07] [01:00] Mina: what's the latency on your hosted rerank for topK=10?
[02:12] Ethan: on our hosted SLA, for a standard rerank profile we see p95 around 120-220ms depending on model size and token length; for optimized low-latency profiles we can get p95 near 80-100ms with batching and KV cache. if you push to dedicated you can get even lower.
[02:29] Liam: those numbers are promising. our SLO target is p95 < 200ms end-to-end. if we keep Elastic prefilter and rerank only top10 that should fit. how about cost rough ballpark?
[02:40] Sofia: cost depends on model choices and qps. a quick calc — embeddings are cheaper per call, rerank is heavier. we'll send a sample cost calc for 10M queries/month in the follow-up. for hosted we show per-token and per-embedding pricing — and there's caching options to reduce unit cost drastically for repeated queries.
[02:57] [01:30] Ethan: demo time — sharing my screen. here's the Redwood Console quickstart: you can create an API key, test embeddings in the playground, and view latency/cost breakdown per route. i'll run a small example.
[03:11] [01:45] Ethan (screen): calling embeddings endpoint — see body: {"input": "red shoes running"}. returned vector length, and here's similarity search with a small dataset. now switching to rerank tab — sending query + 10 doc candidates. note response includes score and highlight snippet.
[03:31] Mina: nice, that explain snippet looks useful for debugging relevance drift.
[03:34] Ethan: yeah it can also return token-level attributions in verbose mode though that does add latency.
[03:40] Priya: about integration — do you prefer we host the vector index or do you offer a managed index?
[03:45] Sofia: we don't host customer indexes by default; typical flow is you host your vector store (Pinecone, Milvus, vector DB) and call our embeddings to compute vectors. we also support direct upserts to a managed index via partners but most customers keep index in their infra.
[03:58] [02:30] Liam: security stuff — we need SAML SSO and audit logs plus control over keys (KMS). does Redwood hosted satisfy that?
[04:05] Sofia: yes — hosted has enterprise features: SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs export, and you can integrate a customer KMS for encryption at rest in private deployments. for Hosted API we support encrypted keys, and we have SOC 2 Type II. i'll attach the security pack.
[04:23] Mina: data residency — some of our traffic must stay within EU. do you have region pins?
[04:29] Sofia: yes we have region routing and you can pin workloads to eu-west and eu-central — that's available on enterprise plans.
[04:36] [03:00] Priya: one thing — evaluation. we have labeled relevance pairs, 5k queries. can you run a small benchmark to show improvement vs our current in-house model?
[04:44] Ethan: absolutely. if you share the 5k labeled pairs we'll run an offline rerank benchmark and return MAP/NDCG and latency numbers. that was one of the next steps we mentioned.
[04:53] Mina: great. also curious about cold-start and caching — when user asks a very long query, how do you handle token length and cost?
[05:01] Ethan: our runtime supports dynamic truncation and you can pick a sequence length cap; for long queries we recommend chunking and retrieval-augmented rerank where the top candidates are preprocessed. caching — prefix and KV caching can avoid recomputing for repeated queries; the Console shows cache hit rates.
[05:16] [03:30] Janelle: small note on engineering integration — we provide SDKs (python/node/go) with sample rerank pipeline; we also provide a Postman collection and a notebook which we'll share.
[05:26] Liam: any gotchas around rate limits and burst for hosted? we have traffic spikes during campaigns.
[05:33] Sofia: hosted has quotas and burst windows; if you need guaranteed throughput you can go Dedicated reserved capacity which gives GPU pools and autoscaling policies. for spikes we also offer burst capacity add-on.
[05:43] Priya: competitors — have you seen customers replace Algolia or Elastic with this pattern? or is it more hybrid?
[05:49] Ethan: typically hybrid. Elastic is still great for filters and fast indexing; customers replace parts of relevance stack with embeddings + rerank to improve semantic recall. some customers use us with Algolia too as a hybrid.
[05:59] [04:15] Mina: ok good. on compliance we're SOC2 and it's a hard requirement for our procurement team.
[04:22] Sofia: noted — we'll include SOC2 report and an answers doc for procurement.
[04:27] [04:30] Ethan: quick technical aside — our rerank endpoint supports two modes: synchronous scoring for request/response and batch scoring for offline scoring, the latter is cheaper for POC evaluation. we also expose a lightweight explain API to help tune prompts.
[04:44] Mina: can rerank use precomputed embeddings to save time if we already have doc vectors?
[04:48] Ethan: yes you can pass embeddings for both query and docs; that can reduce compute because we skip text->embedding step. good for customers with large index and their own emb pipeline.
[04:56] [05:00] Priya: any limits on candidate size? topK?
[05:03] Ethan: we typically accept up to topK=500 for rerank but latency scales; best practice is topK 50-200 and rerank top10 for user-facing queries.
[05:11] Mina: that fits our plan to prefilter down to 200.
[05:14] [05:15] Sofia: ok we're about 10 minutes left — let's recap and list concrete next steps.
[05:19] Ethan: recap: 1) AuroraShare to send sample labeled queries (5k) & a small doc sample 2) Redwood to run offline rerank benchmark with MAP/NDCG and latency 3) Redwood AE to send pricing + security pack 4) schedule POC scoping call.
[05:36] Mina: sounds good. one more question — logging and observability: can we get per-route latency breakdown and cost per call?
[05:43] Sofia: yes the Console provides per-route latency/cost breakdown and token-level counters. we can also stream traces to your tracing system via integrations.
[05:52] Liam: that's useful. please include integration notes for DataDog/Zipkin in the docs.
[05:56] Sofia: will do.
[06:00] [05:45] Priya: ok thanks everyone. if we like the benchmark results we'll move to a short POC with dedicated capacity trial.
[06:08] Sofia: perfect — we'll follow up early next week. thanks for your time.
[06:12] [06:30] (call ends)

Notes about transcription: occasional mis-hearings: "KV cache" appeared as "KV cash" in a segment, and speaker attribution may be slightly off in a few lines.
